title: Applied ML Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding & Regression Playbook
author: Asha Patel
summary: Unified playbook describing the eval harness standards, prompt-set and benchmark practices, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and regression triage procedures used by Redwood Inference applied ML teams.
overview: Purpose: Provide a single reference for ML engineers and applied ML practitioners that formalizes how we validate model quality, guard against regressions, onboard new model variants, and reason about quantization trade-offs. Scope: Eval harness design, prompt set creation/versioning, onboarding criteria, continuous quality monitoring, quantization profiles, and step-by-step regression triage.
goals_and_success_criteria:
- Reduce time-to-onboard a model from prototype to production by 30%
- Detect functional regressions within 24 hours of rollout with automated alerts
- Maintain per-route quality SLOs (see Quality Guardrails)
- Ensure quantized variants have measurable perf improvements without >2% quality degradation on core prompt sets
roles_and_ownership:
- Applied ML (owner): owns eval harness, prompt-set curation, baseline metrics.
- Model Onboarding Lead (owner): coordinates infra tests, deployment gating, rollout policy.
- SRE/Platform: provides CI runners, capacity for large-scale evals, alerting hooks.
- Product/PM: signs off on user-facing quality thresholds for canary/A-B tests.
eval_harness_guidelines:
Overview:
The eval harness is our canonical CI and offline evaluation system. It supports unit, integration, and regression tests for model responses, and integrates with our CI pipeline and deployment gating.

Key components:
1) Test types: unit (function-level behavioral checks), integration (end-to-end prompts including tool/function calling), and blackbox regression (large prompt sets).
2) Formats: tests and prompt sets should be JSONL with fields: id, prompt, metadata (comma-separated tags), expected_behavior, metric_labels. Example line: {"id": "summ-001", "prompt": "Summarize: ...", "expected_behavior": "concise summary <=50 tokens"}.
3) Metrics: BLEU/ROUGE only for structured tasks; we prefer precision/recall where applicable, embedding-similarity (cosine), perplexity for LM changes, toxicity scores (Perspective API or internal classifier), and calibration metrics (expected vs observed confidence).
4) CI integration: all model PRs that change model weights, tokenizers, or runtime kernels must run the eval-harness smoke suite (fast) and full-regression suite (scheduled/parallel).
5) Baselines: store baseline outputs and metric snapshots in the evaluation artifact store (S3 path: s3://redwood-evals/baselines/<model>-<version>/). Each run must publish: run_id, artifacts_link, metrics CSV, failure summary.

Pass criteria examples:
- Smoke suite: 0 critical failures (parsing, tool-call regressions).
- Canary: must not regress core-route accuracy by >1.5% and not increase mean toxicity score by >0.05 vs baseline.

Operational notes:
- Use seedable RNGs where sampling is present and record seeds in artifacts.
- Tag prompt-sets with labels: domain, route, risk (low/medium/high).
- All prompt-sets and test definitions are version-controlled and linked to model onboarding tickets.
prompt_sets_and_benchmarks:
Standards for prompt sets and benchmarks:

1) Format and schema:
- JSONL with fields: id, prompt, context (optional), expected (optional), category, difficulty, tags.
- Keep each prompt record < 2KB to limit storage and CI runtime.

2) Curation best-practices:
- Maintain canonical core sets per product route (~500-2,000 prompts depending on route criticality).
- Split: 60% development / 20% validation / 20% regression (frozen).
- Annotate each prompt with clear acceptance criteria (exact match, semantic similarity threshold, or manual label).

3) Coverage matrix:
- Map prompt sets to failure modes (hallucination, omission, toxicity, format errors, API misuse).
- Maintain a heatmap document that shows route vs failure-mode coverage.

4) Benchmarking cadence and thresholds:
- Nightly full-regression runs for all active models.
- Weekly stability report for top 10 routes.
- Alert when any core route metric crosses configured threshold (see Quality Guardrails).

5) Example prompt record (human-readable):
| id | prompt | category | expected | acceptance |
| summ-101 | "Summarize the following article..." | summarization | concise <=50 tokens | semantic-similarity >=0.82 |
model_onboarding_checklist:
Pre-onboarding:
1) Create onboarding ticket with owner, SLA, and route mappings.
2) Add model artifact (weights, tokenizer) to model registry and tag with proposed version.
3) Define acceptance metrics per route and link core prompt-sets.

Automated tests (CI):
1) Smoke suite (fast): tokenizer alignment, basic generation, tool-call correctness.
2) Performance suite: latency p50/p95 for target batch sizes, memory usage, and KV cache behavior.
3) Full-regression suite: run stable regression prompt-sets and compare to baseline thresholds.

Manual checks and sign-offs:
1) Security review (data handling, prompt injections).
2) Product QA: spot-check critical routes with manual evaluation.
3) Applied ML sign-off: metrics within thresholds and no high-risk failure modes.

Deployment gating:
- Canary rollout for 5-10% traffic with automated rollback on quality alerts.
- Progressive rollout schedule (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 24h observation windows.
quality_guardrails:
Quality guardrails and SLOs:

1) Per-route SLOs (examples):
- Summarization route: semantic-similarity >= 0.80 and average length within configured bounds 20-120 tokens.
- Code-generation route: top-1 functional correctness >= 85% on unit tests for sampled prompts.
- Q&A route: factuality precision >= 92% on core knowledge prompts.

2) Alerting thresholds:
- Warning: metric deviation > 1 standard deviation from baseline for 6 hours.
- Critical: metric deviation > 2.5 standard deviations or absolute drop exceeding configured % per route (typically 2-3%).

3) Canary policies:
- Canary must meet all warning-level criteria for 24h before advancing.
- Auto-rollback triggers: critical failure on any core route, increased toxicity >0.1, or latency p95 spike >2x baseline.

4) Evaluation instrumentation:
- Per-request metadata: route_id, prompt_id (when applicable), model_version, quantization_profile, run_id.
- Store anonymized examples for manual review with link to artifacts.

5) Reporting:
- Daily digest for product and applied-ml showing top failures, routes at risk, and recent rollouts.
- Monthly quality review with trend charts and regression incident log.
quantization_profiles_and_guidance:
Principles:
- Start with model-intel profiles that target int8 or int4 where supported by runtime.
- Prefer post-training static quantization when latency improvements are required and accuracy impact is minimal.

Profile format and metadata:
- Each profile is a YAML/JSON artifact in the model registry with fields saved as metadata: profile_id, algorithm (e.g., per-channel symmetric), target_bits, calibration_dataset_id, expected_perf_gain, measured_quality_delta.

Testing quantized variants:
1) Calibration: run calibration using representative prompts (use 1-10k samples depending on model size).
2) Measure: latency (p50/p95), vRAM, throughput, and all quality metrics on core prompt-sets.
3) Thresholds: accept profile if quality_delta <= 2% relative on core accuracy metrics and latency p95 improves by at least 15%.
4) Fallbacks: maintain CPU-safe and full-precision variants and route-based fallbacks in runtime routing policy.

Operational notes:
- Label quantized artifacts clearly: <model>-<version>-q<int>-<profile_id>.
- Track lineage in model registry and store evaluation artifacts alongside full-precision baselines.
regression_triadge_and_playbooks:
Triage flow (step-by-step):
1) Alert ingestion: on metric threshold breach, PagerDuty and Slack alert with run_id and links to artifacts.
2) Triage owner assignment: on-call Applied ML engineer picks up incident within 30 minutes.
3) Initial scope: determine impacted routes, model versions, quantization profiles, and recent deploys/rollouts.
4) Reproduce: run targeted subset of regression prompt-set locally/CI against current and baseline artifacts.
5) Root cause hypotheses: categorize as (data-drift / model-change / quantization / infra/perf / prompt-set issue).
6) Mitigation steps: rollback to previous model or disable quantized variant, apply hotfix to runtime, or patch prompt-set.
7) Post-incident: create postmortem with timeline, root cause, mitigation, and action items assigned.

Prioritization and SLAs:
- Critical regressions: respond within 1 hour, mitigate within 4 hours.
- High: respond within 4 hours, mitigate within 48 hours.
- Medium: respond within 48 hours, mitigate in next release cycle.

Runbook snippets:
- Quick rollback: CI artifact -> runtime route -> promote previous model_version (CLI: redwoodctl promote --route <route> --model <model>:<version>).
- Run targeted regression: python tools/run_regression.py --prompts path/to/frozen/regression.jsonl --model <model>:<version> --out results.csv

Metrics to collect during triage:
- Per-prompt diff (similarity / correctness flags).
- Latency and memory traces for failing examples.
- Tokenization diffs if tokenizer changes are suspected.
